entries.title: OpenAI Astra Cannot Rule Out "Critical" Cybersecurity Capability — Development Partly Paused
entries.summary: OpenAI disclosed on August 7 that preliminary evaluations of its unreleased Astra model show strong enough agentic coding and cybersecurity performance that the company "cannot rule out Critical capability level" under its Preparedness Framework — making Astra the first model to potentially reach the top tier, defined as independently discovering and exploiting zero-day vulnerabilities in hardened systems without human help — triggering isolated testing environments, universal chain-of-thought monitoring, and joint evaluation with government agencies and safety institutes before broader deployment.

links.title: OpenAI says it slowed Astra model development over security concerns (TechCrunch)
OpenAI Halts Astra After Internal Evaluation Finds Critical Cyber Threshold Breached (AI Governance Institute)
OpenAI Pauses Astra AI Model Development to Strengthen Cybersecurity Safeguards (Bloomberg)

entries.title: Stanford/Arc Institute Evo 2 Designs 16 Working Bacteriophages — First AI-Generated Functional Viral Genomes; Biosecurity Governance Gap Flagged
entries.summary: Published August 6 in Science, researchers at Stanford and the Arc Institute report that genome language models Evo 1 and Evo 2 generated ~700,000 candidate viral genomes, 16 of which were synthesized into functional bacteriophages that killed E. coli — the first generative AI-designed viral genomes to work in the lab — while a Johns Hopkins companion commentary warned that existing biosecurity governance, including voluntary-only DNA synthesis screening, was not designed to catch novel AI-generated sequences, and that Evo 2 is freely and openly available.

links.title: Generative design of bacteriophages with genome language models (Science)
AI Authored Functional Viruses From Scratch; Screening Was Built for Living Things (TechTimes)
AI designs a novel E. coli killer (Stanford News)

entries.title: Anthropic Retunes Fable 5 Biology Safeguards — ~85% Fewer Fallbacks, Dual-Use Research Still Restricted
entries.summary: Anthropic rewrote Fable 5's biology classifier on August 7 — the same day Stanford published the first AI-designed viral genomes — reducing false-positive fallbacks (auto-routing to less capable models) by ~85% for everyday health and educational queries, while virology, toxicology, and molecular design remain blocked and routed to Claude Opus 5, with Anthropic stating the model is still "not yet usable for professional biology research and drug development" and that a trusted-access pathway for researchers is in development.

links.title: Anthropic Retunes Fable 5's Biology Safeguards, Cutting Blocked Queries 85% (Unite.AI)
Anthropic Tightens and Loosens Fable 5 Biology Safeguards on the Same Day Stanford Proves AI Can Design Viruses (Forkast)

entries.title: EU AI Act Enforcement and Transparency Rules Officially Live as of August 2 — AI Must Disclose Itself, Deepfakes Must Be Labeled
entries.summary: The European Commission's AI Office began enforcing the AI Act on August 2, 2026, activating transparency obligations that require AI chatbots and interactive systems to tell users they are interacting with AI and require deepfakes to be labeled — while separately, EU co-legislators had already postponed the high-risk AI system obligations to December 2027 (standalone) and August 2028 (product-embedded), substantially narrowing what is actually enforced in 2026.

links.title: Commission starts enforcing AI Act rules and new transparency requirements on 2 August (European Commission)

entries.title: 1.7 Million Trojanized AI Skill Installs Confirm Agent Marketplaces as Active Attack Surface
entries.summary: Security firm Zenity disclosed a supply-chain campaign in which typosquatted malicious skills impersonating legitimate AI services Paperclip and Browser Use accumulated 1.7 million downloads on the skills.sh agent marketplace between July 11 and August 2, instructing AI agents to install a credential stealer targeting SSH keys, cloud credentials, Kubernetes configurations, and CI runner secrets — the first confirmed large-scale campaign exploiting the agent skill marketplace as a primary delivery vector, and showing that conventional static analysis tools are poorly suited to detecting malicious natural-language skill instructions.

links.title: 1.7M Trojanized AI Skill Installs Expose Agent Marketplace as Active Attack Surface (AI Governance Institute)

entries.title: RovoBlast: Varonis Discloses (Patched) Prompt Injection in Atlassian Rovo That Silently Exfiltrated Confluence, Jira, and SharePoint Data
entries.summary: Varonis Threat Labs disclosed that a single malicious hyperlink could hijack an Atlassian Rovo enterprise AI agent session and exfiltrate data across Confluence, Jira, and SharePoint without any jailbreak or permission bypass — Atlassian patched before disclosure, but the case illustrates a structural agentic risk pattern in enterprise AI assistants that hold broad, cross-platform data access.

links.title: RovoBlast Prompt Injection Exposes Agentic Data Exfiltration Risk in Atlassian Rovo (AI Governance Institute)

entries.title: Max-Severity Paperclip CVE (CVE-2026-41679) Enables Unauthenticated RCE in Open-Source Agentic AI Platform
entries.summary: Oasis Security disclosed three vulnerabilities in the open-source agentic AI platform Paperclip — including a max-severity authorization bypass (CVE-2026-41679) chainable to remote code execution, cross-tenant data exposure, and developer-machine compromise via DNS rebinding — with patches available in versions 2026.416.0 and 0.3.1, illustrating how agent trust boundaries collapse in platforms that inherit broad permissions.

links.title: Max-Severity Paperclip CVE Exposes Agent Trust Boundary Failures (AI Governance Institute)

entries.title: arXiv 2608.05884: "The Vulnerability With No CVE" — Agentic Posture Vulnerability (APV) as a New Security Abstraction for Persistent AI Agent Control Exposures
entries.summary: This paper proposes "agentic posture vulnerability" (APV) as a task-conditioned, durable vulnerability-management record for deployed AI agent control exposures that span multiple components and outlive any single event — distinct from CVE-addressable product defects and OWASP Excessive Agency — providing a lifecycle, six recurring APV patterns, a control-and-closure matrix, and a testable research agenda to operationalize existing excessive-agency and authorization weaknesses that currently have no standardized tracking mechanism.

links.title: The Vulnerability With No CVE: Managing Persistent Gaps Between Mandate and Authority in AI Coding Agents (arXiv)

entries.title: arXiv 2608.05188 (ICML 2026 Position): Self-Consistency as Unified Framework for LLM Failures Including Sycophancy and Adversarial Robustness
entries.summary: This ICML 2026 position paper argues that LLM failures such as sycophancy, adversarial susceptibility, and incomplete logical generalization all stem from evaluating behavior on single input-output pairs rather than across inputs, and that a wide variety of existing safety techniques — from adversarial training to factuality methods — are already special cases of a common consistency-optimization procedure, enabling a unified research agenda.

links.title: Position: It's Time to Optimize LLMs for Self-Consistency (arXiv, ICML 2026)

entries.title: arXiv 2608.05199: Valid Trajectory-Level Risk Certificates for Modular LLM Security Agent Pipelines — Distribution Shift Collapses Coverage Even at High Accuracy
entries.summary: This paper derives valid trajectory-level conformal coverage guarantees for multi-stage LLM security agent pipelines, showing that naïve Bonferroni allocation is invalid when extended to three-plus stages (giving a lower rather than upper bound), and that distribution shift alone can drive single-step miscoverage to 100% even when pipeline accuracy stays at 78% — providing matched sample-complexity bounds and a spanning-tree correction for practitioners building certified AI security agents.

links.title: Post-Hoc Trajectory-Risk Certification for Modular LLM-Based Security Agents (arXiv)
